title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
text: Billee’s one fault was his excessive good nature, while Joe was the very opposite, sour and introspective, with a perpetual snarl and a malignant eye. Buck received them in comradely fashion, Dave ignored them, while Spitz proceeded to thrash first one and then the other.
question: How did Spitz react when the two new dogs arrived in the camp?
options: He ignored them completely
He welcomed them like good friends
He hid from them in the warm tent
He attacked both of them right away
explanation: Цитата: «Spitz proceeded to thrash first one and then the other» доказывает, что Спиц сразу напал на обоих новичков.

text:
The fridge is dark, the night is cold,
I hunt for cheese that's getting old.
My bare feet freeze upon the floor,
I drop a grape and wake the door.
Oh bitter fate, my midnight crime,
Caught snacking one more hungry time!
question: What gets the character caught in the act?
options: The freezing floor
A cold refrigerator
A dropped grape
A barking pet
explanation: Строка «I drop a grape and wake the door» доказывает, что падение винограда выдало героя.

title: Five Children and It
author: E. Nesbit
text: The Vicar was certain a lunatic was on the church-tower—the one who had written the mad letter, and taken the cold tongue and things. Andrew thought it was a “trap”; the cook’s cousin alone was calm. “Great cry, little wool,” said he; “dangerous chaps is quieter.” He was not at all afraid. But then he had a gun.
question: Why was the cook’s cousin so calm?
options: He was a brave lunatic
He knew the children well
He had a gun with him
explanation: But then he had a gun. That was why he was asked...

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
text:
“Mayn’t I sing them just one little song?” he pleaded piteously.
“No, not one little song,” replied the Rat firmly, though his heart bled as he noticed the trembling lip of the poor disappointed Toad.
question: How does Rat react when Toad begs to sing just one song?
options: He happily lets Toad sing.
He feels sorry but still says no.
He laughs at Toad's sad face.
explanation: Rat says "though his heart bled as he noticed the trembling lip" but still refuses.

title: Russian Folk Tales
author: A. N. Afanasyev
text: In front of him stood the Tsar’s palace decked with gold and silver, and at the window the Tsarévna Without a Smile sat and gazed on him straight. What should he do? The light in his eyes turned dark, and a sleep fell on him, and he fell straight into the mud.
question: Why did the poor workman fall straight into the mud?
options: The angry Tsar pushed him down.
He was too tired and fell asleep.
He tripped over a huge sheatfish.
explanation: Текст прямо говорит: «a sleep fell on him, and he fell straight into the mud».

title: Russian Folk Tales
author: A. N. Afanasyev
text:
Then the poor nobleman brought the golden flower out of his pocket, and the goblet, and said, “There is the testimony.”
What could they do? The princesses had to acknowledge their guilt, and the king bade the entrance to the subterranean realm be slated up.
question: Why did the princesses finally have to admit what they did?
options: The king promised them a reward.
They wanted to marry the nobleman.
They got tired of lying to the king.
The nobleman showed solid proof.
Their father forced them to dance.
explanation: Noble brought the golden flower out of his pocket... testimony

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
text: “By no means,” said the Sea Rat frankly. “Such a life as you describe would not suit me at all. I’m in the coasting trade, and rarely out of sight of land. It’s the jolly times on shore that appeal to me, as much as any seafaring. O, those southern seaports! The smell of them, the riding-lights at night, the glamour!”
question: What kind of sailor is the Sea Rat?
options: He only works during the cold winter nights.
He stays close to land and loves the shore.
He travels for months without seeing land.
He spends all his time exploring deep jungles.
explanation: Цитата: «I’m in the coasting trade, and rarely out of sight of land. It’s the jolly times on shore that appeal to me»

text: Dear Diary, today I stared deeply into the human's soul while they ate pizza, using my most tragic starvation face. It totally worked because I got a huge piece of cheese, proving once again that emotional manipulation is my greatest superpower.
question: Why did the human give the pet a piece of cheese?
options: The pet looked extremely sad and hungry
The pet successfully completed a trick
It was time for the pet's regular lunch
explanation: Правильный ответ очевиден благодаря фразе: "using my most tragic starvation face. It totally worked because I got a huge piece of cheese".

title: Five Children and It
author: E. Nesbit
text: “There’s a lady coming,” he said briskly—“for goodness’ sake, get out of the way. Go home—hide—vanish somehow! I can’t be seen with a pack of dirty kids.” His brothers and sisters were indeed rather dirty
question: Why does the grown-up Lamb want his brothers and sisters to hide?
options: He wants to eat all the food alone
He is playing a game of hide-and-seek
He is ashamed of their dirty clothes
explanation: Текст объясняет это прямо: «I can’t be seen with a pack of dirty kids» и «His brothers and sisters were indeed rather dirty».

text: The ancient wizard offered the desperate knight a magical sword of ultimate destiny. Instead of accepting the glowing blade, the knight sighed and asked if there was a cashback option. The wizard dropped his staff in pure shock, muttering that economy in the realm was getting completely out of hand.
question: What does the knight actually want from the wizard?
options: To return the sword for money
To buy a cheaper magic potion
To get a discount on a shield
To learn a new spell for free
explanation: Слово cashback означает возврат денег: «asked if there was a cashback option».

title: Russian Folk Tales
author: A. N. Afanasyev
text: Then the rich peasant began to think: “Heigh-ho! I shall also begin sowing in the winter; possibly I shall have corn as fine.” So he waited to the very day on which the poor peasant in the previous year had sown his corn, went and took from his bins quarters of different sorts of corn, went out into the fields and scattered it all on the snow.
question: Why did the rich peasant scatter his corn on the snow?
options: To feed the hungry birds during the storm
To copy the poor peasant and grow fine corn
To hide his grain from greedy tax collectors
explanation: «I shall also begin sowing in the winter; possibly I shall have corn as fine.»

title: Five Children and It
author: E. Nesbit
text:
“Well then,” said Anthea, “everything we have wished has turned out rather horrid. I wish you would advise us. You are so old, you must be very wise.”
“I was always generous from a child,” said the Sand-fairy.
question: Why does Anthea ask the Sand-fairy for advice?
options: She wants to know how to get rich.
She wants to learn the Ninevite language.
Their previous wishes went badly.
She needs help building a new palace.
explanation: Anthea explains: “everything we have wished has turned out rather horrid. I wish you would advise us.”

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
text:
“Well, never mind what done it,” said the Mole, forgetting his grammar in his pain. “It hurts just the same, whatever done it.”
But the Rat, after carefully tying up the leg with his handkerchief, had left him and was busy scraping in the snow.
question: Why does the Rat start scraping in the snow instead of helping the Mole right away?
options: He is trying to dig a hole to hide from the wind.
He wants to find his lost handkerchief.
He is looking for a place to build a fire.
He wants to find what cut the Mole's leg.
explanation: Rat заметил странный порез и начал раскапывать снег: Looks as if it was made by a sharp edge of something in metal.

text:
Old Joe built a wooden boat to sail the desert sand.
He wore a shiny captain hat and waved his rubber hand.
His loyal hound fell fast asleep upon the empty seat.
Because the ocean moved away down Texas way last week.
question: Why is Joe sailing his boat through the desert?
options: His dog told him to go that way
The ocean moved away last week
He is looking for hidden pirate gold
He wants to catch a desert fish
explanation: Текст объясняет причину прямо: "Because the ocean moved away down Texas way last week".

text:
My alarm clock screams like a metal fan,
I hit the snooze button as fast as I can.
Ten minutes later I jump from the bed,
With coffee in hand and a towel on my head.
Now running for bus while eating my toast,
I always regret what I wanted the most.
question: Why does the speaker have to rush so much?
options: They missed the kitchen
They lost their shoes
They woke up too late
They love morning runs
explanation: Строка 'Ten minutes later I jump from the bed' показывает, что герой проснулся слишком поздно из-за кнопки snooze.

title: Aesop's Fables
author: Aesop
text: A full-grown Bull was struggling to force his huge bulk through the narrow entrance to a cow-house where his stall was, when a young Calf came up and said to him, “If you’ll step aside a moment, I’ll show you the way to get through.” The Bull turned upon him an amused look. “I knew that way,” said he, “before you were born.”
question: How did the Bull react to the young Calf's advice?
options: He listened carefully and tried his idea.
He got very angry and chased him away.
He asked the calf to help him push.
He looked at him with amusement.
explanation: Текст подтверждает это: «The Bull turned upon him an amused look.»

title: Jeeves Stories
author: P. G. Wodehouse
text: Well, of course, nothing is jollier than sweating up the Classics when it’s a hundred in the shade, but there does come a time when you begin to feel the need of a little relaxation; and, by Jove, there are absolutely no facilities for relaxation in this place whatever. And then Steggles got this idea.
question: What do the young men think about studying the Classics in this desert spot?
options: They think it is too easy in the shade.
They prefer reading sermons to classics.
They want to study much harder now.
They are tired of it and want to relax.
They find it extremely fun and exciting.
explanation: Текст говорит: «there does come a time when you begin to feel the need of a little relaxation».

text: Leo told his flatmate, "I am going to feed the monster in the basement, wish me luck." Sam panicked, dropped his coffee, and shouted, "We don't have a basement, what are you talking about?" Leo pointed calmly at the robotic vacuum cleaner bumping into the washing machine. "See? It eats dust and tries to escape every single day."
question: Why did Sam panic?
options: He thought a dangerous creature was in the house.
The washing machine started leaking water everywhere.
Leo broke his favorite coffee mug on the floor.
explanation: Sam panicked because Leo said, "I am going to feed the monster".

text:
A clumsy young baker named Dave,
Baked cakes that belonged in a cave.
They glowed in the dark,
And scared off a shark,
So now he sells rocks to be safe.
question: Why did Dave decide to change his job?
options: He met a friendly shark
He wanted to live in a cave
His cakes were too dangerous
He ran out of sweet flour
explanation: Его кексы «scared off a shark», поэтому он перешел на камни: «now he sells rocks to be safe».
